name: The Extent and Gravity of Sin

objectives.text: Identify from the Bible that all people everywhere have sinned against God
Recall from David's prayer that every sin is first of all a sin against God
Recite Romans 3:23 and explain in their own words what it teaches about every person
Summarize Paul's teaching that Jew and Gentile alike are under sin and the whole world is accountable to God
Explain the catechism's teaching that every sin deserves God's wrath and curse
Explain why James teaches that breaking one command makes a person guilty of breaking the whole law
Compare biblical examples showing that some sins are more heinous in the sight of God than others
Explain why universal guilt means no one can be declared righteous before God by their own works of the law
Describe how encounters with God's holiness in Scripture reveal the seriousness of sin
Analyze how the person sinning, the party offended, the nature of the act, and its circumstances aggravate the heinousness of a sin
Explain the Reformed reasoning that the gravity of sin is measured by the holiness and majesty of the God against whom it is committed
Interpret Jesus' warning about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit within its context in the Gospels
Explain the confessional teaching that no sin is so great it brings damnation on those who truly repent, using Paul as an example
Evaluate claims of sinless perfection in this life using the teaching of First John
Distinguish the Reformed teaching that every sin deserves damnation while sins differ in degree from the Roman Catholic division of mortal and venial sins
Evaluate common cultural ways of minimizing sin against the biblical account of its extent and gravity
Construct an explanation of how universal guilt and the varied gravity of sin together show the need for the gospel offered to all

changes: Merged redundant early-grade universality items (whole world guilty, no one without sin) into a K item, a grade 1 item on sin as against God, and a grade 2 recitation of Romans 3:23. Dropped 'best deeds stained by sin' as belonging to Total Depravity. Reworded 'apply the truth' and 'connect' items into observable explanations anchored in Romans 3:20 and WLC Q152. Added objectives on James 2:10, God's holiness revealing sin's seriousness, perfectionism claims, and the mortal/venial distinction, which absorbed the 'defend the biblical scale' item. Folded the grade 10 'construct a theology' item into the grade 12 synthesis. Corrected confession citations, including WLC Q150 to Q152 and WCF 15.4, and expanded the unpardonable sin passages to their full context.
